articles.title: Spotify’s AI DJ now takes requests
articles.summary: Spotify is allowing subscribers to use voice commands to control which songs are spat out by its AI DJ feature.
articles.body: Spotify is giving users more control over which songs are spat out by its AI DJ feature. Starting today, Spotify Premium subscribers can now use English voice commands to personalize what music they want DJ to play instead of relying on the ever-changing playlist that it curates based on their listening habits. Users can access these new capabilities by pressing and holding the ‘DJ’ button located in the bottom right corner when using the AI DJ feature and listening for a beep. Users can then verbally tell the DJ bot what they want to hear, such as “play me some electronic beats for a midday run,” or “surprise me with some indie tracks I’ve never heard before.” Prior to the update, this button would just randomly switch up whatever song you were currently listening to and didn’t allow users to control what would be played next. Now, Spotify says that users can direct it to play specific artists, genres, and moods. It also borrows some of the quirkier vibe-based music recommendations from the AI Playlist building feature that Spotify launched in beta last year, which creates a tracklist based on text prompts. For example, users can ask the AI DJ to “play me some music to soundtrack my life as a movie.” [Image: If you have a particular track in mind then it may be easier to play it directly, rather than hope that the AI DJ lines it up for you. This new voice command update is currently the only means for users to have any control over what tracks the AI DJ will play, however, which is a bit awkward if you’re using the feature in an environment where you can’t be chatty.

articles.title: Bruce Springsteen fan club founders say political fights, El-Sayed endorsement led to shutdown: report
articles.summary: Bruce Springsteen's endorsement of Michigan's senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed proved the final straw for the Spring-Nuts fan club founders as group shutters.
articles.body:
A Bruce Springsteen fan club couldn't escape the badlands and shuttered over political commentary.

Founded more than a decade ago, the "Spring-Nuts" Facebook group dedicated to The Boss noticed its 18,000 members were no longer focused on his music as they battled against "hateful" online discourse due to Springsteen's public stances and recent endorsement of Michigan's senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed .

"As the world grew increasingly divisive, hostile, those tensions inevitably spilled into our little corner of the E Street world," founders Julie and Howie Chaz said in a statement posted on Sunday, Nov. 8, according to Asbury Park Press .

"What should have been respectful differences of opinion too often deteriorated into personal attacks, bullying, insults, and some genuinely vile and hateful rhetoric."

Springsteen embarked on the "Land of Hope and Dreams" tour earlier this year with the E Street Band and legendary guitarist Tom Morello .

The 20-date tour across North America was slated in response to President Donald Trump and the " No Kings " protests.

"We are living through dark, disturbing and dangerous times, but do not despair – the cavalry is coming," Springsteen said while announcing the tour on social media in February.

"We will be rocking your town in celebration and in defense of America – American democracy, American freedom, our American Constitution and our sacred American dream – all of which are under attack by our wannabe king and his rogue government in Washington, D.C."

He added, "Everyone, regardless of where you stand or what you believe in, is welcome – so come on out and join the United Free Republic of E Street Nation for an American spring of rock 'n' rebellion! I'll see you there!"

"Spring-Nuts" founder Howie Chaz admitted that as Springsteen became "more outspoken about his politics," the group administrators were tasked with a "difficult balancing act" of respecting "his absolute right" while maintaining an ethical online community.

"How could we be a Bruce Springsteen fan community trying to protect that harmony and camaraderie and ignore messages and statements coming directly from the very artist who brought us all together," Howie said.

Springsteen's November endorsement of El-Sayed as "a fighter for our American Constitution" was the final straw for admins.

"Mr. Sayed campaigned with Hasan Piker who openly made horrific statements that America deserved 9/11," Howie said.

"After a Michigan synagogue was attacked back in March, obviously an act of terrorism, Sayed rationalized it by saying 'Hurt people hurt people' standing right next to the antisemitic streamer Hasan Piker who made the despicable 9/11 statement."

His endorsement was "deeply disappointing to us, given our concerns as proud Jews," Julie and Howie said.

"We certainly don't believe Bruce intended for his message to make fans feel unwelcome. But very unfortunately, some of his fans appointed themselves the gatekeepers of who was and wasn't worthy of belonging in the E Street community."

While the group's annual Seaside Serenade and Spring-Nuts podcasts will continue under a different name, the group will rebrand with a focus on music in general, Howie told the Asbury Park Press.

"One thing we want to make absolutely clear is that Julie and I can NEVER thank Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band enough for the decades of music, memories, inspiration, and absolute JOY they have brought into our lives," Howie said on Facebook.

"Bruce has been, and always will be, an enormous part of our personal story and journey. His music has been the soundtrack to so many of the most meaningful moments of our lives, and through Spring-Nuts, it opened doors, created opportunities, and introduced us to extraordinary people and experiences we could never have imagined."

Springsteen's representatives did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

articles.summary: Papai Noel dos Correios 2026 em Juiz de Fora mobiliza padrinhos para atender pedidos de crianças carentes; escolha uma cartinha até 8 de dezembro e realize um sonho.
articles.body:
Correios na Marechal Deodoro em Juiz de Fora — Foto: Mariana Souza/g1

Começou nesta semana em Juiz de Fora a tradicional campanha 'Papai Noel dos Correios' . A ação, que consiste em adotar uma cartinha para presentear uma criança, está atualmente na fase de apadrinhamento.

As cartinhas são escritas por estudantes de escolas públicas , até o 5º ano do ensino fundamental, além de crianças em situação de vulnerabilidade social atendidas por instituições parceiras.

Os interessados têm até 8 de dezembro para acessar o site e escolher um ou mais pedidos que desejam atender. O presente deve ser entregue até o dia 10 do mesmo mês em uma das agências da cidade.

Rua Henrique Dias, n.º 187, no Bairro Benfica;

Avenida Presidente Itamar Franco, n.º 720, no Centro;

Avenida Rui Barbosa, n.º 474, no Bairro Santa Terezinha;

Rua Padre Café, n.º 138, no Bairro São Mateus;

Caso a pessoa prefira escolher a cartinha pessoalmente, basta ir à agência na Rua Marechal Deodoro, n.º 470, no Centro.

Além de Juiz de Fora, outras cidades da Zona da Mata e do Campo das Vertentes recebem a campanha.

Confira o endereço das agências nas cidades da região participantes:

Além Paraíba: seleção e entrega na Rua Coronel Oscar Cortes, n.º 91.

Barbacena: seleção e entrega na Rua José Bonifácio, n.º 23.

Carandaí: seleção e entrega na Praça Capitão Policarpo Rocha, n.º 46.

Carangola: seleção e entrega na Avenida Coronel Maximiano, n.º 36.

Muriaé: seleção e entrega na Praça Coronel Pacheco de Medeiros, n.º 260 e também na Rua Itagiba de Oliveira, n.º 16.

Cataguases: seleção e entrega na Avenida Astolfo Dutra, n.º 44.

São João del Rei: seleção e entrega na Avenida Tiradentes, n.º 500.

Santos Dumont: seleção e entrega na Rua Prefeito José Maria Pitella, n.º 33.

Ubá: seleção e entrega na Avenida Vereadora Rafael Girard, n.º 64.

Viçosa: seleção e entrega na Avenida Bueno Brandão, n.º 578; e na Praça Emílio Jardim, n.º 79.

A campanha surgiu em 1989, por iniciativa dos próprios funcionários. Eles recebiam cartinhas de crianças endereçadas ao Papai Noel ou destinadas ao Polo Norte, e começaram a comprar presentes para atender aos pedidos.

Com o aumento do número de cartas, os Correios abriram a campanha para toda a população em 1997. Desde então, qualquer pessoa pode adotar uma cartinha e presentear uma criança no Natal.

articles.title: Dustin Hoffman Denies Sexual Misconduct Allegations in New Memoir but Admits He May Have Made Women ‘Uncomfortable’
articles.summary: In his book ‘Look at Me,’ Hoffman makes reference to 2017’s #MeToo movement, likening it to McCarthyism
articles.body:
Dustin Hoffman opens up about serious allegations made against him in new memoir Look at Me

In the book, he denies allegations of sexual misconduct made against him amid 2017's #MeToo movement

"I'm sure it's true that in my life, especially forty years ago, I made some women uncomfortable," writes Hoffman, claiming that "'uncomfortable' is a subjective emotional state"

In his new memoir, Dustin Hoffman opens up about serious allegations that have been made against him over the years.

While Hoffman, 89, does not address specific accusations of sexual misconduct , which include claims from six different women that surfaced in 2017, Look at Me (on bookshelves Nov. 10) includes a chapter that delves into the actor's work in the controversial 1971 movie Straw Dogs and his 1982 hit Tootsie .

"I'm sure it's true that in my life, especially forty years ago, I made some women uncomfortable," writes the two-time Oscar winner. "But 'uncomfortable' is a subjective emotional state. What is crass and offensive to one person, another individual might find hilarious, or enlivening, or even sort of cozy."

Hoffman writes extensively about his sense of humor, calling himself "out there," in the memoir. "I love a so-called dirty joke. I am 'a Borscht Belt flirt,' as Bill Murray once put it. That's not the same thing as pressuring someone to do something they didn't want to do."

The father of six alludes to the #MeToo movement that began in 2017, writing, "When a reckoning started making its way around the internet, and tearing through Hollywood, I thought it was a very good thing. I knew by then that plenty of women had put up with way too much for way too long in my industry. Not for a second did I worry that anything negative would be said about me, because the idea of taking something from someone sexually that they didn't want to give... it's just not something I've ever done."

In 2017, three women spoke to Variety about their alleged encounters with Hoffman, accusing him of sexual harassment, sexual assault and exposing himself to a minor. While the actor issued a public apology to one accuser, his lawyer called the assault allegations from two of the women "defamatory falsehoods" at the time.

Earlier that year, three women separately accused Hoffman of sexual harassment, with one claiming she was assaulted when she was 17 years old as a production assistant on Death of a Salesman in 1985, the same production on which a second woman said Hoffman groped and assaulted her. A third woman claimed Hoffman propositioned her during a pitch meeting. No lawsuits or criminal charges were brought against Hoffman.

Likening the allegations of sexual misconduct against men in power to the McCarthy era of the early 1950s, in which Hollywood figures and other notable Americans were blacklisted for affiliations with communism, Hoffman writes his "entire life changed" amid the reckoning. "There was no innocent until proven guilty. There was no 'proving' anything at all."

He continues, "The whole thing was so crazy, I was sort of bewildered by how to defend myself... or if I should even try. I didn't want to be fighting against something that I thought was important. I didn't want to be on the wrong side of my own values. The only problem was that things were being said about me that just weren't true."

In Look at Me , Hoffman writes that he has "learned a lot from" Lisa , his wife since 1980, "about men and women and the different ways we perceive a given situation. It took me years (decades?) to understand that flirting with every woman I met was not okay."

He continues, "It's not that Lisa has ever doubted my love or my commitment. (Many times over the years, she has noticed me staring at a pretty woman, and said, 'Dusty, would you like me to introduce you?') She knows who she's dealing with. She fell in love with a guy with a bawdy sense of humor who is obsessed with sex and is always looking for attention."

He adds that it took "an embarrassingly long time to grasp that if I was flirting or my jokes were too dirty, people who were not my wife might think I was being inappropriate. I know I'm harmless, she knows I'm harmless, but if you'd never met me before, would you know? ... I'm not looking to humiliate or offend anybody. I'm not a person who gets off on having power, or pressuring people to do things. To be perfectly honest, I never thought of myself as a person with power in the first place."

The Rain Man star also writes, "Is it possible that I've been guilty of insufficient empathy? That I was too self-involved to correctly perceive what the people around me were feeling all the time? Sure. Of course."

He concludes the chapter, "If you don't feel the same way, then you are different from every other human being I've met in this life. Male or female."

Hoffman most recently appeared on the big screen in the movies Tuner and Diamond . His memoir Look at Me will be available wherever books are sold on Nov. 10.

articles.title: Attack on Titan 3 confirms a major change that puts Eren Yeager's legacy in a new light
articles.summary: Eren Yeager may have been the face of Attack on Titan for years, but the upcoming third game is giving fans a chance to experience the brutal world of
articles.body: Eren Yeager may have been the face of Attack on Titan for years, but the upcoming third game is giving fans a chance to experience the brutal world of Titans through a completely different set of eyes. Koei Tecmo is introducing a customisable Scout who will take centre stage in the new adventure. The change does not erase Eren's legacy. Instead, it gives players a personal role in one of anime's most emotionally charged stories, with familiar characters, dangerous missions and a fresh character-driven ending.Attack on Titan 3 lets players create their own heroThe biggest change in Attack on Titan 3 is the introduction of a player-created protagonist. Rather than controlling the entire experience through Eren's perspective, players can design their own Scout and become part of the Survey Corps.The customisation options offer plenty of room for creativity. Players can adjust facial features, hairstyles, body types and outfits. They can also add smaller details, including glasses and chokers, to give their characters a distinct appearance.However, the new hero will not be fighting alone. The character will join familiar faces such as Mikasa Ackerman, Armin Arlert and Levi. Players can also build relationships with other members of the regiment at headquarters, with these connections affecting squad performance during missions.Combat is also receiving attention. The developers have refined the omni-directional mobility gear, allowing players to move through Titan-infested areas with greater control. Special Exterior Missions will add another layer of strategy, putting players in charge of squad decisions, supply bases and battlefield retreats.The game is scheduled to arrive on December 10, 2026, for PC, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X|S.Attack on Titan 3 promises a different ending for its new protagonistThe new character also brings an interesting narrative change. According to producer Hideo Suzuki, the game will cover the complete story, from the fall of Wall Maria to the events of the fourth season. However, players will experience those events through their own Scout.In an interview with Crunchyroll published on October 30, Suzuki explained why the team chose this approach.“So in the previous game, the story hadn’t ended. To conclude our game, we had to come up with some kind of ending to it, and therefore, we had this “what-if” scenario... For this game, since we’re covering the entire story, there’s already an ending to it. So it wouldn’t make sense to have our own ending to the story in a game. Because this story would be told from the perspective of your main character, it’s not like a “what-if” type of ending. But there is an ending for your particular character.”This means Eren's established fate will remain intact, while the custom Scout will receive a separate conclusion to their personal journey.For longtime fans, this could make familiar events feel different without changing the original story. articles.title: ‘Yellowstone’ star Dawn Olivieri chose Arkansas ranch life over LA to reclaim her ‘freedom’
articles.summary: "Yellowstone" star Dawn Olivieri reveals the career dry spell that drove her to leave LA for a 160-acre Arkansas ranch and animal sanctuary.
articles.body: "Yellowstone" alum Dawn Olivieri is opening up about the turning point that drove her to leave Los Angeles behind and build the life that she actually wanted on a ranch and animal sanctuary in rural Arkansas. During an interview with Fox News Digital, the 45-year-old actress, who is starring in the second season of Angel Studios’ post-apocalyptic drama "Homestead: The Series," shared how she became disillusioned with Hollywood during a lull in her career after years of chasing acting success. "I realized it wasn't giving me what my dream of what it was supposed to give me," Olivieri said. 'VAMPIRE DIARIES' STAR IAN SOMERHALDER SAYS LEAVING HOLLYWOOD FOR FARMING 'SHIFTED MY LIFE FOREVER' "It wasn't cooperating," she continued. "I didn't have offers, just like falling out of my phone. I went through a dry spell, and I was like, ‘Wow, so this is an illusion.'" "I kind of saw through the veil and once I saw through veil — I realized in that moment, I have to make some decisions about my life that makes me happy — [it] isn't always waiting by the phone, losing my power, waiting for someone to hire me," Olivieri recalled. "I'm like, ‘Oh, what am I doing?’" 'HOMESTEAD' STAR BAILEY CHASE SAYS CALIFORNIA VACCINE PLANS WERE 'FINAL STRAW' THAT DROVE FAMILY OUT OF LA "I just jumped ahead," she explained. "I go, ‘If I did make all this money and was successful, what would I do with it?’ Well, I would move to the country and have horses and OK, well, I guess let me go do that. Let me, let me see what. And so I did that with nothing. Which wasn't the dream part, but in actuality, it was what was always meant to happen because I moved toward my own authenticity." In 2022, the actress left LA and bought a 160-acre property outside Mena, Arkansas. The following year, Olivieri founded the nonprofit organization Moon Mountain Sanctuary and Rescue, which rescues and rehabilitates hundreds of horses and other animals. 'LIONESS' STAR JILL WAGNER RAISES DAUGHTERS IN TENNESSEE TOWN OF 800, WHERE HORSES AND BUGGIES STILL ROAM During an August appearance on the "Let's Talk Local" podcast, Olivieri said she is currently living in a camper on the property while she continues to build and expand her ranch and animal sanctuary. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Olivieri reflected on the unexpected result that came from her decision to leave Hollywood and create the lifestyle she had always envisioned, explaining that giving up control of her acting career ultimately improved it. HOLLYWOOD STAR SOUNDS ALARM OVER DISAPPEARING JOBS AS PRODUCTIONS FLEE CALIFORNIA "I think in that moment, I became a better human being," she said. "I became a better actress for sure. I started working way more than I did when I was in LA waiting for the job, waiting for the call." "And I moved to a land of no mirrors is what I called it," Olivieri continued.. "I went into a deep relationship with the core of my being versus what everything looked like, what I looked like." "And I would recommend that move to anybody," she added. Olivieri's "Homestead: The Series" co-star Charles Esten, who joined her for the interview, agreed that letting go of the pressure to land the next role can sometimes have the opposite effect in Hollywood. "It’s not just Hollywood, it’s the whole world that — but especially Hollywood — can smell that desperation of, ‘I need this to get that,’" Esten said. WATCH: ‘YELLOWSTONE’ STAR DAWN OLIVIERI TRADED LA FOR ARKANSAS RANCH "The second you sort of don’t hold so tightly and you have sort of more philosophy of abundance and let it a little looser. Or another way is just give it up," he continued. "I don’t mean give it up by quit doing it, but give up the need and the desperation on it. And then they finally go, ‘Hey, you want to come do a show?’" "Yeah, literally, that’s what happened," Olivieri replied. Olivieri pointed out that many other actors faced a dramatic decrease in work opportunities in recent years due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2023 SAG-AFTRA and the Writers Guild of America (WGA) strike. 'VERONICA MARS' STAR JASON DOHRING TRADED HOLLYWOOD FOR FARMING "But I had a very clear decision that I was willing to give up this identity of being an actress," she said. "And maybe if I had to sell farm fresh eggs on the side of the road, I would do that just to keep my freedom." "Homestead: The Series" follows survivors living at a fortified prepper compound in the Rocky Mountains known as The Homestead after a nuclear attack on LA plunges the country into chaos. Olivieri plays Jenna Ross, the wife of Ian Ross (Neal McDonough), the wealthy prepper who established the Homestead, while Esten portrays Cain Ross, Ian's estranged brother. After Ian is incapacitated and later dies, Jenna is pushed into a leadership role and struggles with how to protect the community while maintaining her compassionate approach toward outsiders. Meanwhile, Cain arrives at the Homestead after Ian's injury and takes a much more hardline approach to survival and leadership. In season two, which premiered on Nov. 3, Jenna and Cain find themselves in conflict over how the compound should be run as resources dwindle. Olivieri was part of the cast in the 2024 theatrical movie "Homestead," which introduces the story. Esten joined the cast for the first season of "Homestead: The Series," which picks up where the movie left off. The show also stars Kevin Lawson Emmanuel McCord, Jesse Hutch and Betzaida Landín. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Olivieri and Esten shared their thoughts on why more Americans are increasingly interested in homesteading, growing their own food and moving away from big cities. "People are thinking about it because everything else is becoming toxic in all truth," Olivieri said. "Our food system has gone toxic because of profit. Our way of life in a city has become toxic because of overpopulation potentially or, again, I really think the root of it is profit and money and commerce." "In this state of government, being open and available is just a nicer experience," she added. "It is for me anyway." Esten drew a contrast between Olivieri's homesteading and the gritty survivalism depicted on "Homestead: The Series." "Dawn's homesteading that I've noticed is beautiful," he said. "Our version of homestead is very extraordinary necessity, fear-based. Plant these fences and Dawn's is the opposite of that. Dawn's very open and welcoming and saving animals that need it and welcoming other folks on." After Olivieri embraced rural life and stopped waiting for Hollywood to call, the actress went on to land major roles in Taylor Sheridan's universe. Olivieri played Claire Dutton, the widowed sister of James Dutton (Tim McGraw), in 2021's "1883." From 2022 to 2024, Olivieri portrayed Sarah Atwood, the corporate strategist brought in by Market Equities who becomes involved with Jamie Dutton (Wes Bentley), in "Yellowstone." She has a recurring role as CIA officer Amber Whalen on "Lioness" and most recently made a guest appearance in "The Madison." While speaking with Fox News Digital, Olivieri weighed in on what she believes sets the prolific creator apart from others in Hollywood. "He doesn't ask for permission to do anything," she said. "He listens to his North, his guide, and he writes textured, powerful human beings, especially women, which I find is very, very rare." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "He writes them like it's coming from inside of himself," Olivieri continued. "I've talked to him about this because he will write things for a strong woman that makes you read it on the page and then look around, like, ‘Is someone watching me? How are you in my head?’" Olivieri recalled asking Sheridan how he was able to write female characters with such insight. "I went to him and I said, ‘How do you know how to do that?’ And he told me point blank, he said his mom was a strong woman," she remembered. "So he had a very, very, very close example of how strong women move and what they do and how they think and the way that they talk." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "He writes things poetically," she continued. "He has texture. There's magic in the way that he writes and it's just undeniable. And he agrees he's tapped. He'll sit and wait for the muse and the muse will share the story with him. And that's how he writes." "They are a conduit for some energy that flows through them. And he has told me that that's exactly what happens for him." articles.title: Russell Brand, Katy Perry video resurfaces, sparking concern after conviction
articles.summary: Russell Brand held up an "obey" sign as Katy Perry spoke to a reporter, with the 2010 clip resurfacing and sparking concern after his rape conviction.
articles.body:
A red carpet interview with former couple Katy Perry and Russell Brand is resurfacing, and some viewers are looking at Brand's behavior through a new lens.

The red-carpet exchange is drawing fresh scrutiny after a London jury convicted Brand of rape and sexual assault ⁠ Nov. 5. A judge sentenced the British comedian, 51, to 10 years and six months in prison ⁠ Tuesday, Nov. 9.

The 2010 video shows a reporter asking Perry which Academy Award winners she was happiest for following the awards show, at Vanity Fair's annual Oscar party March 7 outside the Sunset Tower Hotel in West Hollywood, California⁠.

Perry and Brand stopped to talk to British morning show "GMTV," and when Brand starts to give his take on the Academy Awards, Perry laughs.

Brand tries to answer the question himself and holds up a small tag that read "obey." "You didn't watch it!" she said. Brand insists he had. When Perry uses an expletive (as seen in the video below), he tells her, "don't swear."

After Brand holds up the tag, the reporter turns back to Perry and asks how she dealt with him. "He's actually hilarious," Perry replied. "He leaves me speechless."

Photographs from that night⁠ shows Brand also holding the tag toward the cameras as he posed beside Perry. A logo resembling artist Shepard Fairey's Obey logo appears next to the word.

The video has sparked a larger conversation online, with one X user (@Xx17965797N) describing Brand as using the tag "to control her." Some viewers who revisited the footage after the verdict called the exchange "disturbing" in the comment section.

"Mind you he used to use an 'obey' tag on katy perry every time she wasn't agreeing with him," wrote @notwhomstfarted. "imagine the horrors he did behind closed doors…"

USA TODAY reached out to Perry's representatives for comment.

Six women accused Brand of sexual offenses dating from 1999 to 2009. At his 2026 trial in London, jurors convicted him of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault and acquitted him of the three remaining charges. He has denied the allegations against him.

What Katy Perry said about her marriage to Russell Brand

Perry and Brand married in India in October 2010⁠. In a 2013 interview with Vogue ⁠, Perry said she often invited him to join her on the road and tried to get home when she could.

"He didn't like the atmosphere of me being the boss on tour." Perry said. "So that was really hurtful, and it was very controlling, which was upsetting."

Fourteen months after their wedding, Brand sent her a text on New Year's Eve 2011 saying he wanted a divorce, Perry told Vogue. At the time of the interview, she said, it was the last she'd heard from him.

The Crown Prosecution Service ⁠ said Brand committed sex crimes against four women between 2004 and 2009, before he married Perry. Prosecutors agreed to leave the marriage out of their opening statement after his lawyers objected. Brand later told jurors that marrying Perry had brought him "staggering fame."

Contributing: Liza Esquibias, Brendan Morrow, USA TODAY

articles.body: Country music legend Dolly Parton’s initiative to encourage children to read has reached an extraordinary milestone, with her Imagination Library having gifted more than 300 million free books to children since its launch in 1995. Adding to the celebration, the Country Music Association (CMA), Belmont University, The Walt Disney Company and the Nashville Convention & Visitors Corp (NCVC) have come together to contribute a combined $1 million towards the programme.The announcement followed the star-studded television special, CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton, which honoured the singer's remarkable musical journey and her contribution to generations of fans. While the evening celebrated her legacy as a performer and songwriter, the donation highlighted another side of Parton's life: her commitment to childhood literacy and education.Dolly Parton launched the Imagination Library in 1995 inspired by her fatherThe story behind the Imagination Library is deeply personal. Parton was inspired to start the initiative by her father, who was unable to read or write. Wanting to ensure that children had access to books from an early age, she launched the programme in her home county of Sevier, Tennessee, in 1995.What began as a local initiative soon grew into an international book-gifting programme. Its central idea remains simple: give young children access to books and encourage them to develop a love for reading before they begin school.Today, the Imagination Library operates across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and the Republic of Ireland. It has gifted more than 300 million books since its inception and mails over three million age-appropriate books to children every month.Under the programme, every enrolled child receives one book every month from birth until the age of five, completely free of cost to their families.Disney, CMA and partners contribute $1 million to Dolly Parton's initiativeThe latest $1 million contribution brings together four organisations that joined hands to celebrate Parton's legacy. The Country Music Association, Belmont University, The Walt Disney Company and Nashville Convention & Visitors Corp collectively announced the donation following the television tribute.CMA CEO Sarah Trahern said the event was designed to bring people together, much like Parton's music has done over the years. She highlighted how the performances and support from partners had helped turn a celebration of the singer into a meaningful contribution towards children's literacy.CMA incoming CEO Brittany Schaffer also acknowledged Parton's influence through her music, philanthropy and generosity, adding that the initiative would help carry her legacy forward for future generations.Belmont University President Dr Greg Jones said that a love of learning could open doors and shape the future of young people. He expressed gratitude for the opportunity to celebrate Parton's life while helping put more books into children's hands.Nashville Convention & Visitors Corp President and CEO Deana Ivey also spoke about the singer's connection with the city, describing her as one of Music City's greatest ambassadors. She said the organisation was proud to support a cause that remained close to Parton's heart.Jeff Conyers, President and Vice Chair of The Dollywood Foundation, said the donation was a meaningful way to celebrate Parton's life by investing in the dreams of future generations.A star-studded musical tribute celebrates Dolly Parton's legacyThe fundraising announcement followed CMA Presents I Will Always Love You: A Celebration of Dolly Parton, a special featuring several prominent country music artists performing some of her most memorable songs.The performances included Ella Langley singing Jolene, Kelsea Ballerini performing Here You Come Again, Ashley McBryde taking on Coat of Many Colors and Darius Rucker performing Two Doors Down.Other highlights included Lady A performing Islands in the Stream, Carly Pearce and Kristin Chenoweth joining forces for 9 to 5, and Little Big Town performing Light of a Clear Blue Morning.Carrie Underwood led the full cast in a performance of I Will Always Love You, while Zac Brown presented Butterfly in a vocal duet with Dolly Parton.The television special is now available to stream on Disney+ and Hulu.How Dolly Parton's book programme continues to reach millions of childrenThe Imagination Library is the flagship initiative of The Dollywood Foundation, a non-profit organisation that works with thousands of local programme partners to make the book-gifting model possible.While the foundation manages the partnerships, resources and systems behind the initiative, local partners help create awareness and raise funds to cover the wholesale cost of books and their delivery.This collaborative model has allowed Parton's original dream to reach millions of households across different countries. More than three million books are now mailed every month, giving children an opportunity to build their own home libraries from an early age.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Anupam Kher 'completely overwhelmed' by Sweden's response to 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend'; says, 'People came up to me with tears in their eyes' after Stockholm premiere
articles.summary: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has shared glimpses from the Stockholm premiere of Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, saying the warm reaction of
articles.body: Veteran actor Anupam Kher has shared glimpses from the Stockholm premiere of Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, saying the warm reaction of Swedish viewers left him overwhelmed. Anupam Kher, who voices Jatayu in the film, posted a video showing audience members shaking hands and chatting with him after the screening.Anupam Kher’s note on the Stockholm premiere‘Ramayana’ reached theatres on 5 November, just in time for Diwali. It had premieres across the world and got mixed reviews from critics, but it has done well at the box office.Anupam Kher wrote a long note on X and Instagram about the Sweden event. “Extremely happy to share these visuals from the Swedish premiere of Ramayana: The Rise of Legend in Stockholm. I began my speech with a sentence in Swedish: “Jag är mycket glad att vara här i Stockholm i kväll.” — “I am very happy to be here in Stockholm this evening.” And I truly was. After 41 years and 556 films in India, it was also special to share that I have become a small part of Swedish cinema for the first time with Out of Fashion,” he wrote.Anupam Kher's message of the epic travels across bordersThanking Anurag Bhushan, India’s Ambassador to Sweden, for the introduction, Anupam Kher said he felt proud to be part of the film by voicing Jatayu. “The Ramayana is not only a story from India; its message of love, sacrifice, family, duty and the triumph of good over evil speaks to people across borders, languages and generations. It was moving to see this timeless Indian epic being celebrated in Sweden,” he wrote.Audience left the actor emotionalAnupam Kher said the response after the film moved him deeply. “When the film ended, people came up to me with tears in their eyes, shaking my hand and thanking me for telling the story of the Ramayana and for playing Jatayu. I was completely overwhelmed. It filled me with immense pride to see a film like this come out of India and connect with audiences here,” he wrote.He congratulated the film’s team and ended his note with, “Proud to be Indian. Jai Shri Ram!”About ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Nitesh Tiwari has directed it, and Namit Malhotra and Yash have produced it on a very large budget. The first part covers Rama’s birth, upbringing, marriage and vanavas. It closes with Ravana abducting Sita and Rama vowing to defeat him. The second part is set to release for Diwali 2028.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Toukie Smith, ‘227’ actor and Robert De Niro’s former partner, dies at 74
articles.summary: Toukie Smith, a model, actor and mother of twins with ex-partner Robert De Niro, died at 74, her children announced.
articles.body: Toukie Smith, a model, actor and mother of twins with ex-partner Robert De Niro, died at 74, her children announced. The former “227” sitcom actor died on Nov. 4 after “a long, courageous battle with multiple sclerosis,” according to a statement released by her children, Airyn and Julian, whom she shared with De Niro. Smith was also the sister of legendary fashion designer Willi Smith, who died at 39 in 1987 from complications from AIDS. Toukie Smith also modeled for him, as well as for other luminaries like Hubert de Givenchy and Patrick Kelly. “As the sister of the late, legendary designer Willi Smith, Toukie shared in a remarkable family legacy that helped shape American fashion and culture,” her children wrote. “She was a model, muse and collaborator, not only to her beloved brother but to other trailblazing luminaries of the era, including the illustrator Alvaro, Jean-Paul Goude, Patrick Kelly and Antonio Lopez,” the statement continues. “Her beauty, grace and unmistakable presence helped pave the way for generations of Black models and designers in fashion.” Smith also played artist Eva Rawley on the hit NBC sitcom “227” starring Marla Gibbs, which ran from 1985 to 1990. She also appeared in multiple episodes of the classic ‘80s show “Miami Vice.” She and De Niro were partners from 1988 to 1996, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Airyn and Julian were conceived by in vitro fertilization and delivered by a surrogate mother. De Niro has five additional children with three other women. “Toukie was a force of nature,” her children wrote. “She left an indelible mark on our hearts and on everyone lucky enough to know her.” What Was Toukie Smith’s Cause of Death? The actor and model died following a “long” battle with multiple sclerosis, according to a statement by her two children. It’s not clear how long she had the autoimmune condition, but her children said in their statement that she died after a “long, courageous battle.” Toukie Smith and Robert De Niro at a benefit honoring Willi Smith.Ron Galella / Ron Galella Collection via Getty What Is Multiple Sclerosis? Multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune condition that affects your central nervous system due to your immune system mistakenly attacking the protective sheaths that surround the nerves in your brain and spinal cord, according to Cleveland Clinic. There are almost a million adults in the United States living with the condition, per the Cleveland Clinic. Symptoms of MS include the following: Double vision or vision lossMuscle weaknessNumbness or abnormal sensationsFatigueLoss of balance or coordinationMuscle stiffness and spasmsDifficulty with memory, concentration, learning and judgmentMood changesDizzinessDifficulty regulating bladder There isn’t a single tool to diagnose someone with MS, which can sometimes make detecting it difficult for doctors. “It can take time before you receive an official MS diagnosis,” according to the Cleveland Clinic. “You may need to make several trips to see your provider before you know for sure. This happens because MS symptoms can look like or happen with several other common conditions.” While there is no cure for multiple sclerosis, there are treatments available to minimize symptoms and flare-ups. Still, MS can lead to disability, especially over time, and can be fatal in rare cases, according tot he Cleveland Clinic.

articles.title: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More
articles.summary: Four years ago, Johnny Depp’s fans and detractors descended on the sleepy town of Fairfax, Virginia, to cheer or jeer the actor in his ugly defamation case a...
articles.body:
Four years ago, Johnny Depp's fans and detractors descended on the sleepy town of Fairfax, Virginia, to cheer or jeer the actor in his ugly defamation case against ex-wife Amber Heard. Now, when local cinema operator Mark O'Meara probes his patrons about "Ebenezer," a new take on "A Christmas Carol" featuring Depp as the coldhearted miser Scrooge, he's met with decidedly less intensity about the embattled star's first major movie role in nearly eight years.

"Some people can't wait. They love Johnny Depp. And others are just like, 'Meh,'" says O'Meara, who owns Fairfax's University Mall and Cinema Arts theatres. "I don't think it's a polarizing thing."

"Ebenezer" isn't expected to ignite the box office à la "Michael," a musical biopic about a controversial figure. The Dickens adaptation, which opens on Nov. 13, is tracking a modest debut of about $20 million domestically and another $20 million overseas from 63 markets. But O'Meara doesn't get the sense the public sees Depp as persona non grata, even though the actor's career has been derailed by personal drama, including domestic abuse allegations leveled by Heard.

Paramount, meanwhile, is betting that moviegoers have been missing Depp, whose last Hollywood outing was 2018's "Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald." (He was forced by Warner Bros. to exit the "Harry Potter" spinoff series in 2020 after losing a libel case against the British tabloid The Sun, which called the actor a "wife beater." Depp won the subsequent defamation trial in the U.S.) An April 2026 study by the National Research Group suggests his fans never turned on him. Participants ranked Depp among the top 10 actors — ahead of Tom Hanks and behind Margot Robbie — who "would make you most interested in seeing a new movie in a cinema in the future."

"Audiences don't care. He's still one of the biggest movie stars on the planet," says Kevin Goetz, founder and CEO of audience research firm Screen Engine/ASI. "That, to me, is very telling about how often Hollywood perpetuates its own self-fulfilling prophecies."

As Hollywood has kept a distance, Depp has remained a popular figure around the world, receiving career achievement and tribute awards from international film festivals and retaining a $20 million brand deal with Dior. Onscreen, he has appeared in underseen indies like the 2020 drama "Minamata" and the 2023 period piece "Jeanne du Barry," and he directed the 2024 biopic "Modì, Three Days on the Wing of Madness." And Depp's fans have been vocal on social media, supporting the actor through his professional struggles and bizarrely rallying in 2021 to nominate "Minamata" for the Oscars first (and only) fan favorite award.

Lately, the town seems willing to forgive Depp. His next film is Lionsgate's 2027 action thriller "Day Drinker," co-starring Penélope Cruz. Meanwhile Disney is looking into "Ebenezer" and the potential backlash, before greenlighting another "Pirates of the Caribbean" movie, according to sources. Depp has said he's open to returning to the franchise , but he noted "the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note."

"Ebenezer" doesn't need to electrify the masses to justify its price tag. Given the uncertainty, Paramount cautiously spent $38 million to produce the Dickens tale. Depp was paid $5 million, a fraction of what he's earned on prior studio movies, with the promise of bonuses tied to box office performance. Marketing expenses were around $50 million, including stops at San Diego Comic- Con where the actor made a surprise appearance, dressed in character, and threw handfuls of candy at the foot of attendees. (Paramount declined to comment on budgets.) Directed by Ti West, known for the "X" horror trilogy, "Ebenezer" spins the oft-told yarn of the curmudgeonly businessman who is visited by the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future.

"I'm optimistic for a few reasons," says Regal's CEO Eduardo Acuna. "Even though this story predates him, it feels like the character was written for Johnny Depp. And it's good IP from a very distinctive filmmaker."

Cinema operators like Acuna suggest the box office haul will speak less to Depp's appeal and more to the movie's quality. After all, there's been no shortage of takes on "A Christmas Carol." Scrooge has been a staple of holiday moviegoing for decades, with popular versions including the 1951 classic with Alastair Sim and 1988's "Scrooged" with Bill Murray. The most recent entry, Disney's 2009 "A Christmas Carol," starring Jim Carrey, brought in $325 million against an overinflated $200 million budget.

"It's a story that's been told a number of times, so it'll be more about whether this one is compelling," says Classic Cinemas CEO Chris Johnson. "I don't know if I've heard anyone saying they won't see it because of Johnny Depp. The public seems to be pretty forgiving."

For Depp, embodying a misanthrope like Scrooge — in the trailer, he's seen scaring villagers and being stingy with Christmas bonuses — jibes with the other offbeat or unlikable characters he's spun into the stuff of contemporary cinema classics. His real-life rebellious persona has helped sell his most famous roles, from the chaotic Captain Jack Sparrow from "Pirates of the Caribbean," eccentric Willy Wonka from "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory" and the mercurial Mad Hatter in "Alice in Wonderland."

"Johnny's image was built on being a bad boy," Goetz says. "He ain't America's dad. We don't want him to be that."

articles.title: Céline Dion head bangs with Jack Black at Metallica concert in the Sphere
articles.summary: Who knew Céline Dion was a secret metalhead?
articles.body: Who knew Céline Dion was a secret metalhead? The 58-year-old singer and her 16-year-old twin sons, Eddy and Nelson, rocked out alongside actor Jack Black at Metallica’s concert at Sphere in Las Vegas on Nov. 7. A fan video that went viral showed Dion dancing and playing air guitar as the legendary heavy metal band performed on stage. Just a few feet away, Black vigorously nodded his head and pointed his fingers in the air in time with the music. Wes Zirkle, who shot the video, attended the concert with his college best friend Ben to celebrate their 51st birthdays. The pair weren’t too shocked to see Black thrashing in the stands, but Dion? “I was really surprised to see Céline Dion like really, really into this concert,” Zirkle tells TODAY.com. The fan reaction to his video showing the unlikely duo sharing a love of Metallica has been “a lot of fun,” Zirkle adds. One fan commented, “I was so focused on Jack Black I totally almost missed Celine Dion. A sentence I never thought I’d say.” “The next duet we need,” another joked. Dion, whose public outings were limited in recent years after she was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome diagnosis, is on temporary break from her triumphant record-breaking comeback Paris residency. The concerts resume in May 2027. Dion shared images from the Metallica show, which showed her posing with Metallica members James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Rob Trujillo. “Thank you James, Lars, Kirk and Robert and everyone from the @Metallica organization for the warm welcome! We had such a wonderful time seeing you at the Sphere. We absolutely loved the show,” she wrote, adding a devil horn hand gesture emoji. Metallica responded in the comments by posting three black hearts. Dion also shared a cute pic of her and her sons posing with Black at the concert. The multi-Grammy winner revealed her love for Metallica in February when she named a few musical acts on her most current playlist in an Instagram video. After the “My Heart Will Go On” singer shared that Metallica was her son Eddy’s “favorite” band, she did a hilarious imitation of Hetfield scream-singing his ferocious lyrics. Metallica’s initial series of dates for its “Life Burns Faster” residency at Sphere ran from Oct. 1 through Nov. 7. The band’s residency resumes in January 2027 and wraps in March 2027.

articles.title: Broncano hace autocrítica tras su entrevista a Santiago Abascal en La Revuelta: "Me arrepiento de muchas cosas"
articles.standfirst: El presentador ha respondido a todas las preguntas en las inmediaciones del Teatro Albéniz
articles.summary: El presentador ha respondido a todas las preguntas en las inmediaciones del Teatro Albéniz
articles.body: David Broncano ha admitido que se equivocó en el formato de entrevista que le planteó a Santiago Abascal. El presentador de 'La Revuelta' ha sido claro con lo sucedido el pasado lunes 9 de noviembre en el Teatro Albéniz durante la grabación de la entrevista con motivo de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. De hecho, en la entrada a la grabación del martes 10 con Ada Colau, admitió de entrada que no estaba bien con el resultado final: "Estoy triste porque creo que no lo hice bien. No lo hice bien ayer". "Creo que me equivoqué con varias cosas, con cómo se hizo y demás. Y pues estoy triste porque no me gusta...", siguió diciendo antes de que se acercaran más medios allí presentes. De hecho, hizo autocrítica ya que admite que igual no tendría que haber renunciado a muchas cosas, entre ellas el humor: "Me arrepiento de muchas cosas, posiblemente tenía que haber utilizado la comedia más, como hago siempre, pero era complicado. También sé que había mucha gente que me decía que con políticos no hagamos bromas." Al ser preguntado por la imagen que dio Santiago Abascal en el programa, se sinceró separando su opinión política con lo transmitido por el entrevistado: "Abascal lo hizo bien, la verdad. Ellos, tanto él como como la gente de comunicación del partido, (...) lo digo a nivel estratégico, creo que lo han hecho bien porque ellos nos pidieron venir con su público, con gente elegida por Vox". "Esa es la clave de todo", señala el cómico sobre la importancia del público en el desarrollo de la entrevista. Una reflexión que continuó: "Para mí es la clave de cómo salió la entrevista porque nosotros aceptamos hacerlo con público seleccionado por Vox porque yo pensaba, evidentemente fui demasiado ambicioso, posiblemente vanidoso y me extralimité en mis capacidades, pensaba que eso podía evitar que luego ellos si no salía la entrevista como querían o que no... con nuestro público les podía llevar a excusarse en eso, que no les hemos dejado hablar, que el público les ha silvado, que les ha abucheado y demás" Una reflexión que finaliza: "Yo pensé que quería quitarles esa cosa, que sé que a veces lo hacen desde Vox y pues me equivoqué, porque en la práctica cuando empezó la entrevista vi, todos lo visteis, que era muy desigual y era muy injusto. Para el público también es por qué le están aplaudiendo cada cosa". De hecho, reconoce que no le gustó cómo estuvo: "Estuve incómodo conmigo mismo, cuando me di cuenta que había generado un ambiente raro y que había generado una situación que creo que no merece una entrevista a un responsable político, en cuanto a que esté tan sesgada de cara a la reacción del público y demás". Y hace autocrítica: "Yo mismo me tiré toda la entrevista diciendo 'me he equivocado, he pensado que era buena idea pero la he cagado'. (...) Veía muchas veces que Santiago estaba hablando y yo estaba pensando por dentro: 'Tío, eres tonto, lo has hecho mal, esto no tiene sentido'. Entonces, tampoco me permitía responderle con la velocidad que habría que haberlo hecho". Un análisis que continuó dando pinceladas con cómo vió al líder de Vox en el programa: "Igual que dije que Abascal estratégicamente lo hizo bien ayer y comunicativamente también, tuvo mucho plomo, digamos que muchas de las cosas que dijo cuando las analizas despacio son muy cuestionables, pero lo hizo bien técnicamente. Formalmente, digamos". Y ante alusiones, lo comparaba con el presidente del Gobierno: "Con Sánchez pasó un poco parecido. Ayer con Abascal, hay muchas cosas en las que todo el mundo sabe que tenemos grandes diferencias, pero creo que lo llevé a un camino... una vez que pasó lo del público, me di cuenta, lo llevé a un camino excesivo porque le quité toda la comedia y toda la distensión de algunas cosas que creo que habría estado bien". Además, son muchas las críticas que ha recibido el presentador de La Revuelta por las entrevistas a los políticos y reconoce: "Yo no he querido hacer ninguna de estas entrevistas. Entiendo que haya muchos periodistas y muchas periodistas que no les haga especial gracia, que haga yo una entrevista así, pero no es una decisión mía, no he peleado yo por entrevistar a los políticos". Justo antes de admitir que no lo hizo bien: "Esto es un muy buen marrón que me ha caído al estar en televisión pública en el programa con más espectadores de la cadena y que ha sucedido así, que yo intentaba hacer con responsabilidad. Intentar hacer el servicio público que se supone que hay que hacer en la cadena, en La 1 y desde luego ayer no fue el caso".

articles.title: Ableton Live 13 announced with a step sequencer, new drum synth, and more
articles.summary: Live 13 is one of the biggest updates to Ableton’s music-making suite in years, adding a step sequencer, new drum synth, and more.
articles.body: Today, Ableton announced Live 13, which is expected to arrive in early 2027 with a slew of new features. Most of the changes are seemingly minor on paper, but when combined, they make for the biggest update to the digital audio workstation (DAW) in years. The feature most likely to draw attention is the addition of a proper step sequencer. While Ableton’s Push controller had a dedicated step sequencer, and you could effectively use the piano roll as one, the desktop app never included one. Ableton didn’t phone this feature in either — it’s a powerful sequencer. You can change velocity, timing, chance, length, and repeats for each step in the grid. Each track can have its own length, playback rate, and direction, letting you create something complex and evolving. [Media: The addition of ARA plugin support will also likely excite pro producers and vocalists. This means compatible plugins can now be used directly on audio in the DAW. For example, pitch correction and time-stretching tool Melodyne previously required you to import audio from Ableton into Melodyne, then render it back out to a track in your DAW. Now it can clean up messy vocal takes directly in Live’s UI. Ableton has also added a new mixer view that lets you see all the loaded devices on a track in a compact vertical view. Here you can drag and drop them between tracks, or copy and paste them. It also makes it much easier to navigate a sprawling 30-track session quickly at a glance. My personal favorite new addition is Looplet, an experimental looping instrument with four playheads and a ton of options for manipulating your audio. It offers granular processing, filtering, pitch and speed control, and each playhead can be routed to individual tracks for additional processing. It’s a powerful tool for ambient and soundtrack work. The full list of new features is sprawling, so here are just a few more highlights: * A new drum synth with more than 20 different models across nine categories spanning classic drum machines and experimental abstract percussion. * Capture now includes not just MIDI notes but automation as well. * Contextual browsing lets you swap instruments and presets directly in the device view, reducing the need to open the main browser. * Multiband racks for processing different frequencies through different effect chains. * A bread-and-butter transient shaper for tightening up drum sounds. * Envelope clips on return tracks for automating effects. * Racks can now have up to 32 macros and custom mapping curves. * Custom layouts on Push 3 for combining mixers, note grids, step sequencers, and more.

articles.title: 'Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace' trailer out: Salman Khan takes on Chinese troops in Galwan-inspired film; says, 'Let's sort this s**t, bro'
articles.summary: The trailer of ‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace’ was released today.
articles.body: The trailer of ‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace’ was released today. It gives a first proper look at the war drama starring Salman Khan and Chitrangda Singh. Directed by Apoorva Lakhia, the film is inspired by the events in the Galwan Valley.‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace’ trailerThe trailer shows the life of a soldier and the sacrifices made by those who serve the country. It also points to the emotional cost of war for the families waiting at home. Alongside the action, the film appears to focus on the human side of the story.Salman Khan in an action-heavy avatarSalman Khan plays a soldier who faces Chinese troops, and the trailer is packed with action. He is seen taking on the opposing forces in intense hand-to-hand combat and holding his ground in fierce clashes.One of the standout moments comes when Salman Khan tells his Chinese counterpart, “Let’s sort this s**t, bro!”Chemistry with Chitrangda SinghSalman Khan makes a strong impression in the action scenes, while his chemistry with Chitrangda Singh brings an emotional layer to the story.The Galwan clash behind the filmThe film was earlier titled ‘Galwan’. It is inspired by the clash between Indian and Chinese troops in the Galwan Valley in eastern Ladakh on June 15, 2020. The fighting killed 20 Indian soldiers, and it was the deadliest India-China face-off in more than four decades.Salman Khan rejects government interference rumoursEarlier at the 'Maatrubhumi' event in Mumbai, Salman Khan dismissed speculation that the film was changed under official pressure. “Naa ke hum China ke against jaa rahe hai…ya humari government ne hum pe pressure dala hai ke iska script change karo, rewrite karo…yeh sab bakwas hai. Not true at all (Neither are we taking a stance against China, nor has our government pressured us to change or rewrite the script. All these rumours are completely baseless and untrue).”He described the film as a human story about soldiers and their families. “So isme ko negative forces nahi hai. Bas halat hai negative. They like each other, but koi situation aata hai toh nation comes first, and both the sides are trying to solve this (There are no negative forces in the film; it’s the circumstances that are difficult. They like each other, but when a situation arises, the nation comes first. Both sides are simply trying to find a way to resolve the situation).”'Maatrubhumi' release date and cast‘Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace’ is produced by Salman Khan Films and releases in theatres on December 4, 2026. Besides Salman and Chitrangda, the film stars Mukesh Rishi, Ankur Bhatia, Zeyn Shaw and Abhilash Chaudhary, with Vijay Raaz as the narrator.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Considera que 'La Revuelta' incurrió en "errores graves" al convertir un espacio de entretenimiento en un programa político sin el rigor exigible
articles.body: El Consejo de Informativos de Televisión Española (TVE) ha reclamado que se asuman responsabilidades por la entrevista que David Broncano realizó este lunes al líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, en 'La Revuelta'. En un comunicado, el órgano ha calificado de "errores graves" tanto el cambio de público habitual como el abandono de la esencia del programa, basada en el humor y el entretenimiento, y ha reconocido que la emisión les hizo sentirse "muy incómodos". "La Revuelta' de anoche nos hizo sentir muy incómodos", comienza el comunicado del Consejo de Informativos de la televisión pública, que considera que el espacio de David Broncano se convirtió en un programa informativo, pero sin el rigor que debería garantizar un espacio de estas características. A su juicio, alguien dentro de RTVE permitió que la entrevista al líder de Vox se presentara como una conversación "seria" sin que se cumplieran las condiciones profesionales que exige el tratamiento informativo de una entrevista política. La intervención de Santiago Abascal provocó un cambio evidente en el tono habitual del programa. El líder de Vox aprovechó su presencia en el espacio para desplegar algunos de los principales argumentos de su discurso político, con ataques al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, al que volvió a calificar de "dictador", además de negar la violencia machista y el cambio climático y calificar la situación migratoria de Ceuta de "invasión". Por su parte, David Broncano se mostró incómodo ante algunas de las declaraciones del dirigente político y este martes ha reconocido públicamente que se equivocó al abordar la entrevista a Santiago Abascal. El Consejo de Informativos aclara que su comunicado no pretende analizar "si se debería haber hecho y cómo se hizo" la entrevista, pero sí considera que una entrevista política, especialmente durante un proceso electoral, debe realizarse desde los servicios informativos y por profesionales de la información de RTVE. Además, el órgano defiende que este tipo de contenidos debe contar con producción "100% interna", algo que, según denuncia, no sucedió en esta ocasión. "Alguien de RTVE permitió que esta entrevista se presentara como 'seria", señala el comunicado, que concluye con una petición expresa de responsabilidades: "Por eso creemos que alguien debería asumir las responsabilidades". La reacción del Consejo de Informativos añade así presión sobre la dirección de RTVE después de una entrevista que ha generado controversia tanto por el contenido de las declaraciones de Santiago Abascal como por el formato elegido para abordar una conversación política en un programa concebido para el entretenimiento.

articles.title: Thomas Markle allegedly cut off ankle monitor after child sexual abuse material arrest
articles.summary: A Florida judge revoked Thomas Markle's bail after he allegedly cut of his ankle monitor. Markle Sr. was arrested Nov. 6 and charged with possession of child sex abuse material.
articles.body: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, allegedly cut off his ankle monitor after being released from federal custody. During an emergency hearing Tuesday, Markle, 82, was remanded back into federal custody. The US Attorney said it's clear "even with medication" Markle remains agitated. Markle's ankle monitor had been cut off and stabbed in an intentional way to disable it, prosecutors told the judge. "He allegedly cut the bracelet off at 1:45 a.m. last night. Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli wrote on X. "We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law." Markle had been released on bond from federal custody Friday following his arrest on a charge of possessing child sexual abuse images. He was initially placed under house arrest.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian faces furious backlash as shoppers demand refunds over $148 advent calendar
articles.summary: Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering full refunds after shoppers slammed its $148 advent calendar filled with hair ties, bobby pins and keychains.
articles.body: Kim Kardashian’s Skims is offering refunds after shoppers slammed its $148 advent calendar over an assortment of "cheap" hair accessories and keychains. The 12-day calendar — which included hair ties, scrunchies, clips, bobby pins, key chains and a compact mirror, according to the product description — drew massive criticism from content creators and social media users as unboxing videos began to go viral. "People buying the skims advent calendar for $150 just to get this has me rolling on the floor," one user wrote on X, alongside a photo of the contents of the calendar. HAILEY BIEBER STRIPS DOWN FOR KIM KARDASHIAN'S SKIMS IN RED-HOT NEW CAMPAIGN "A $148 for a bunch of cheap plastic and hair ties. So she makes a $147 profit? Just another scam," another wrote. "For SKIMS to be a CLOTHING brand and not include a single piece of clothing in the SKIMS advent Christmas calendar is crazy and ridiculous actually," another social media user wrote. "150$ for Bobby pins, scrunchies and tree ornaments WOW." Others dubbed the company simply as, "Skams." One person pointed out that the advent calendar was labeled specifically as a box of accessories, writing, "Paying for ‘Accessories’ and getting mad when its just accessories is hilarious as f--- lmaooo." Another wrote, "On the website they listed all the things that will be in the box, I don’t understand the clout people are trying to chase." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS In a statement, Skims acknowledged the complaints, saying it had contacted every purchaser to offer a full refund or credit toward other products. "We’re aware of the feedback some customers have shared about the Skims Advent Calendar, and we’ve listened carefully," reps for Kardashian and SKIMS said in a statement to Page Six. The spokesperson said that since "the calendar didn’t meet expectations," the company has "personally contacted every customer who purchased the calendar and offered them a choice of a full refund or a Skims credit to put towards other products." Since its launch in 2019, Skims has drawn attention for its various, buzz-generating products. articles.title: 511 quintals of Chhappan Bhog offered to Maa Annapurna on Annakoot
articles.summary: Varanasi’s Maa Annapurna Temple marked Annakoot Mahotsav with 511 quintals of Chhappan Bhog; over 10 lakh devotees attended, prasad served.
articles.body: Varanasi: The Annakoot Mahotsav was celebrated with grandeur and devotion at the Maa Annapurna Temple on Tuesday. The special darshan of the golden idol of Maa Annapurna, which began on Nov 6, concluded with the Maha Aarti on Tuesday.After the Maha Aarti performed by Mahant Shankar Puri, the temple doors of the goddess were closed for one year.On the occasion of Annakoot, Chhappan Bhog was offered to Maa Annapurna during the midday Bhog Aarti. This year, a total of 511 quintals of food items were offered in the temple. The grand offering included both cooked and uncooked preparations, with 40 varieties of sweets and 20 varieties of savoury items. A special attraction of this year was the suran laddoo in the bhog.Devotees offered prayers to the goddess for prosperity, abundance and well-being. After the Chhappan Bhog Aarti, Mahant served prasad to the devotees. A large number of devotees gathered to receive the Mahaprasad.The preparation of the Annakoot prasad starts from the day of Dussehra Sthapana Puja. Around 121 artisans prepared the offerings this year, including nearly 30 women artisans.Temple manager Kashi Mishra said that a large number of devotees from India and abroad visited the temple during the five-day darshan period. More than 10 lakh devotees visited the temple and offered prayers, and thousands received Mahaprasad on the day of Annakoot. The temple administration made well-organised arrangements for prasad distribution, keeping the convenience and safety of the devotees their priority.A team of doctors was also deployed for the convenience of devotees during the darshan period. The medical team provided on-the-spot treatment to thousands of devotees.The temple premises were decorated with colourful lights and fragrant flowers for the Annakoot festival. articles.title: We read Sofia Franklyn’s memoir about her falling out with Alex Cooper so you don’t have to
articles.summary: The “Daddy Gang” is finally getting to hear from the co- “founding father” of “Call Her Daddy.”
articles.body: The “Daddy Gang” is finally getting to hear from the co- “founding father” of “Call Her Daddy.” Sofia Franklyn, who co-created the famous podcast with Alex Cooper, released her memoir “Daddy Issues” on Tuesday, in which she details her falling out with her now ex-friend. The duo shot to viral fame in 2018, when the podcast was still under Barstool Sports. It became known for candid conversations about commonly taboo topics for women to discuss publicly, including raunchy sex stories. But the two professionally split up in 2020, news that initially shocked their listeners. Cooper went on to host the podcast solo, eventually moving it to Spotify and now SiriusXM in lucrative deals that helped propel her to mainstream success. Meanwhile, Franklyn, who is an influencer with over 619,000 Instagram followers, launched her own podcast titled “Sofia with an F.” Over the years, rumors had circulated about what exactly happened between Franklyn and Cooper. Here are some of the biggest claims in Franklyn’s 240-page book. Warnings from others in Cooper’s orbit Growing up in Utah with a single mom, Franklyn writes about struggling to find a clear path. She was arrested three times: once for using a fake ID and twice for underage drinking. Eventually, she left to start anew in New York City, largely to escape an abusive relationship. But her early days in the city were far from ideal. She lived with her aunt and was working at Morgan Stanley in a job under a toxic boss who she claims harassed her regularly. She eventually moved into her own place that she could barely afford and found herself feeling extremely lonely. Until she met Cooper. A random girl Franklyn befriended in a ride share connected her to Cooper and her childhood friend, Lauren, who were looking for a third roommate. Cooper and Franklyn ended up becoming inseparable, with Lauren largely out of the picture as she spent much of her time with her boyfriend. But one night, Franklyn writes, Lauren and her shared a rare evening in the apartment alone together. That’s when Lauren asked Franklyn whether she thought it was weird that Cooper “tossed” her aside. “You showed up and it was like I never existed,” Franklyn said Lauren told her, which prompted Franklyn to apologize. Lauren also told Franklyn that Cooper “uses you because you’re hot, to like, go to parties and stuff.” At the time, Franklyn wrote that she felt defensive of her friendship with Cooper and did not think of it as “using” her. But later, another close friend of Cooper’s from childhood also seemingly warned her that Cooper was not going to stick with her. Muji, known to early “Call Her Daddy” listeners as “Milfhunter,” worked on the podcast with the duo. He told Franklyn that Cooper “doesn’t have friends. I’ve watched it happen since high school.” When Cooper abruptly fired Muji, Franklyn said he told her: “She’s gonna f--- you.” An alleged firing attempt, secret raise and IP disagreement Cooper and Frankyn’s stars rose quickly at Barstool, as the two took creative control of their show with company founder Dave Portnoy’s blessing. But Franklyn started to feel things change after the Barstool holiday party. That night, she felt “insane anxiety,” drank excessively and fought with Cooper. An angry Cooper told Franklyn she was “rude” and “aggressive” toward her at the party and that everyone, including Portnoy, had noticed and wanted to fire her. Franklyn says she wanted to apologize to Portnoy for her behavior, but was told not to by Cooper. When she finally did say something, Portnoy appeared to dismiss it, saying “the girls got in a fight.” It wasn’t until later, Franklyn writes, that she learned Cooper used the party as a way to negotiate a raise for herself. Muji purportedly told her that Cooper said, “If I have to put up with her, I need more money.” She got the raise: $20,000 more than Franklyn every year. “She didn’t tell you because she didn’t want you to know she tried to get you fired,” Franklyn said Muji told her. In 2020, when the duo was negotiating their new contract together, Franklyn wrote they sent Barstool an email with a new proposal in which they asked for “50/50 split of all revenue derived from Barstool’s exploitation of the property (i.e., advertisers, sponsors, merch, etc.)” and a “minimum guarantee — $1M each, per year.” The negotiations centered around the IP for “Call Her Daddy,” which Barstool Sports owned and could technically continue without Franklyn or Cooper attached. Amid their talks with Barstool, Franklyn said she and Cooper agreed their goal was staying together. They even came up with a spin-off podcast if the negotiations fell through, titling it “The Fathers.” “We’re being corny as s---, but it’s because we’re both blissed out on the plan and our future — we don’t know how Barstool will respond, but we know that staying together is more important than losing the IP, or whatever they may threaten. What is the name without us?” But in the end, Franklyn was ousted as co-host. Portnoy called Franklyn to tell her that Cooper had met with him separately and proposed going on without Franklyn. “She came to me with a plan, and I needed an episode. There’s no clear favorite,” he told her, according to Franklyn’s memoir. “You could always have your own show, and we promote the shit out of it like we did with Call Her Daddy. I think it would be huge.” Portnoy also said Cooper had hired her own lawyer and claimed that Franklyn had been “the one that’s been dragging this on, and she’s been ready to sign this thing.” Franklyn claims Cooper subsequently locked her out of their shared social accounts and posted a 52-minute YouTube break-up video called “The Truth about Call Her Daddy” in which she described Franklyn as a “liability.” Six years later, the video is still up and has amassed 4.6 million views. Representatives for Portnoy and Cooper did not respond to requests for comment on Tuesday. Cooper’s alleged legal threat The book opens with a scene in which Franklyn’s book agent calls her to say she received an angry call from Matt Kaplan. Kaplan, a Hollywood producer, married Cooper in 2024. The couple co-founded the Unwell Network, a subsidiary of the media company Trending. Franklyn writes that her agent told her Kaplan said Cooper would sue. Representatives from Unwell told the New York Times that Kaplan “never discussed the book’s claims or any intent to sue the author with Verve.” A representative for Kaplan did not respond to a request for comment on Tuesday. Verve, Franklyn’s literary agency, also did not respond to a request for comment.
